'''Donal B. O'Shea''' is a Canadian [[mathematician]], who is also noted for his bestselling books.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.americanscientist.org/bookshelf/pub/scientists-nightstand-donal-oshea |title=Scientists' Nightstand: Donal O'Shea |publisher=[[American Scientist]] |date=2008-05-20 |access-date=2016-11-14}}</ref> He served as the fifth president of [[New College of Florida]] in [[Sarasota, Florida|Sarasota]], from July 1, 2012, until June 30, 2021. He was succeeded by [[Patricia Okker]] on July 1, 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ncf.edu/news/president-okker-assumes-leadership-of-ncf/ |date=2021-07-01|access-date=2024-05-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220810042110/https://www.ncf.edu/news/president-okker-assumes-leadership-of-ncf/ |archive-date=2022-08-10 |title=
President Okker assumes leadership of NCF |last=Weingarten |first=Abby |website=[[New College of Florida]]}}</ref>  Before coming to New College, he served in various roles at [[Mount Holyoke College]], including professor of mathematics, dean of faculty, and vice president for academic affairs.<ref name="heraldtribune1">{{cite web|author=Christopher O'Donnell |url=http://www.heraldtribune.com/news/20120415/mathematician-deemed-perfect-fit-as-next-new-college-president |title=Mathematician deemed perfect fit as next New College president – News – Sarasota Herald-Tribune – Sarasota, FL |website=Heraldtribune.com |access-date=2016-11-14}}</ref><ref name=":0" />  

O'Shea graduated with a [[B.Sc.]] from [[Harvard College]],<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=https://www.ncf.edu/directory/listing/donal-oshea/|title=Directory {{!}} Donal O'Shea|date=2015-12-31|work=New College of Florida Directory|access-date=2018-03-15|language=en-US}}</ref> and received a [[Ph.D.]] in mathematics from [[Queen's University at Kingston|Queen's University]] in [[Kingston, Ontario]] in 1981; his thesis, titled ''On μ-Equivalent Families of Singularities'', was written under the direction of Albert John Coleman.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|108818|name=Donal B. O'Shea}}</ref>

==Bibliography==
Some of his best known books are:<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goodreads.com/author/show/83902.Donal_O_Shea |title=Donal O'Shea (Author of The Poincaré Conjecture) |website=www.goodreads.com |access-date=2016-11-14}}</ref>
* ''The Poincaré Conjecture: In Search of the Shape of the Universe''.<ref>{{cite book|url= https://books.google.com/books?id=9D-SiaG2FV4C |author=Donal O'Shea|title=The Poincaré Conjecture: In Search of the Shape of the Universe|publisher=[[Bloomsbury Publishing]]|year=2009|isbn=9780802718945}}</ref>

The book has consistently received good reviews.<ref>{{cite news|author=Ian Pindar |url=https://www.theguardian.com/books/2008/nov/29/poincare-conjecture-donal-o-shea |title=Review: The Poincaré Conjecture by Donal O'Shea &#124; Books |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |access-date=2016-11-14}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200801/tx080100037p.pdf |title=The Poincaré Conjecture and Poincaré's Prize : Review |website=Ams.org |access-date=2016-11-14}}
</ref>
* [[David A. Cox]], [[John B. Little (mathematician)|John Little]], and Donal O'Shea: ''Using algebraic geometry'', [[Graduate Texts in Mathematics]], vol. 185, Springer-Verlag, 2005. 
* [[David A. Cox]], John Little, and Donal O'Shea: ''Ideals, varieties, and algorithms: an introduction to computational algebraic geometry and commutative algebra'', 3rd. edition, Springer Verlag, 2007.
